newsitem.title: USA: U.S. workers saving more for retirement - study.
newsitem.headline: U.S. workers saving more for retirement - study.

text.p: U.S. workers are saving more for their retirements, but they still will not have enough money to lead their desired post-work lifestyles, according to a survey released on Tuesday.
Average annual retirement savings rose to $2,388 during 1996, an 11 percent increase from 1995 and a 34 percent jump from 1994, the study showed.

The increase is not enough to close the large gap between savings and retirement living expectations, which have also increased. Expectations among full-time workers for annual retirement income rose almost 8 percent last year, according to the study conducted by Colonial Life and Accident Insurance Company and Employers Council on Flexible Compensation.
Workers age 25 to 34 are saving $1,761 annually, compared to $3,529 in the 45 to 64 age bracket, the study showed. Expectations for annual retirement income rose from $24,372 to $26,256 last year.
According to the study, a thirty-year-old worker would need to save $662 more each month than they are now to be able to afford the desired level of retirement living.

Only half of all workers over 45 say they have an adequate retirement plan in place, the survey of 1,000 U.S. workers showed. One in five said they had given little thought about saving for the future.
